subject: PrivDeploy IaC: BOM & dependency ownership check-in
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, eng-team@helios-health.com
Cc: Priya Narayanan <priya@helios-health.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: PrivDeploy IaC: BOM & dependency ownership check-in

Hi all,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, attaching the initial Bill of Materials (BOM) for the Helios private deployment along with an operator compatibility matrix and the sanitized Helm values we plan to ship. Our ask for this thread is narrow: agree owner and gating requirements for every third-party module/operator in the BOM and confirm any blocking compatibility gaps before we branch the private-deploy tree.

Quick context/high-level checklist:
- BOM lists Terraform modules, Helm charts, Ansible roles, container images and a note on provenance (digest where available).
- We want every module to have an "owner" (team or person) and a CI gate: e.g., image-signature verification, pinned provider versions, and automated SBOM generation.
- Operator compatibility matrix highlights tested K8s versions and whether we run in an air-gapped mode.

Action items for thread: please reply with:
1) Ownership annotations or proposed owner for any rows you currently own.
2) Any compatibility blockers (e.g., operator doesn't support node-local DNS in our VPC configuration) or tests we must add to the gate.
3) A short note on whether the existing CI pipeline (PRIVDEP-412) can perform policy checks + SLSA attestation collection, or if we need to extend it.

Attachments: priv-deploy-iac-bom.csv, operator-compat-matrix.xlsx, helm-values-sanitized.yaml

I'll compile replies into a single list and propose a minimal gating policy (PR + pipeline steps) by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Lukas
Senior Infrastructure PM
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-team@helios-health.com, Priya Narayanan <priya@helios-health.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: BOM & dependency ownership check-in

Lukas — thanks for pulling this together. I skimmed the BOM and ran a quick compatibility pass. High-level notes:

1) Ownership
- terraform/aws-vpc-module: assign to "networking-team" (Vanessa) — responsible for AZ mapping and route table modules.
- helm/ingress-nginx: assign to "platform-services" (me) for the pinned version and values.
- operator/postgres-operator: assign to "db-ops" (Karthik) but they need a compatibility confirmation for our internal FQDN scheme.

2) Blocking compatibility items
- postgres-operator: current v1.7.x uses svcAccount permissions that conflict with our PSP/OPA policy in air-gapped mode. We need an RBAC exemption or an init job that preps secrets.
- metrics-operator image: not signed in our private registry. CI must include cosign verification before promotion to the "canary" registry.

3) CI gates and tests to add (minimal set)
- SBOM generation step that outputs SPDX and SLSA provenance attestation for any image we build or reference.
- cosign signature verification for pulled images; fail the stage if an image has no valid signature.
- terraform plan step runs with provider-version lockfile enforcement (terraform lockfile).
- Helm chart lint + values schema validation (we should add JSON schema checks for the sanitized values).

Notes on approach:
- For operator compatibility, propose a small test harness that runs operator CR creation in a trimmed staging cluster matching Helios' CNI + network policy settings. We should capture failures as structured test artifacts.
- Ansible roles: ensure idempotence by running converge twice in CI (apply + apply) and fail on divergent state.

I'll open a few PRs with suggested changes: one to add cosign to the build matrix, one to add a SBOM step, and one to annotate the BOM with suggested owners.

-Mina
Staff SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-team@helios-health.com, Priya Narayanan <priya@helios-health.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: BOM & dependency ownership check-in

+1 to Mina's items. A couple of operational additions from the networking perspective:

- Terraform modules: add a post-plan step that performs a diff of route tables and NAT placements and uploads the diff to our internal audit bucket. This lets Helios reviewers see the expected egress topology before apply.
- Egress allowlist: for air-gapped installs we need a documented minimal egress list for images (registry mirrors) and for policy updates (apt/yum repos). I'll add a section to the BOM for "egress-exceptions" with owner = networking-team.
- K8s node labels and taints: some operators refuse to run on nodes with certain taint combinations. Add an operator field in the BOM for "node-constraints" so the installer can auto-apply a taint/label strategy during bootstrap.

Schedule note: I can take lead on finalizing the egress list and the route-diff audit work if we target next Tuesday (2026-09-21) for the first PR to land into the private-deploy main branch.

Vanessa
Network Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Narayanan <priya@helios-health.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, eng-team@helios-health.com
Date: 2026-09-15T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: BOM & dependency ownership check-in

Thanks, everyone — this is helpful. From Helios' side:

- We accept the ownership assignments as proposed (networking-team and db-ops owners are fine).
- For the RBAC issue with postgres-operator, we can allow a scoped exemption for the private deployment only; will open an internal request and share the ticket number by EOD tomorrow.
- Regarding cosign and SBOM: we require signature verification in our pre-production gate. Would it be possible for Redwood to run the cosign validation in CI and provide an artifact we can reference (the cosign signature + sbom link)?

Canary ask: before we move to full prod, can we run a single-node canary in Helios' staging VPC with the same NAT/route settings and a truncated dataset to validate bootstrapping and operator lifecycle? If Redwood can own the canary run and provide the CI artifacts (plan diffs, SBOMs, cosign attestations, and operator test artifacts), we can sign off.

Priya
Head of Platform Engineering
Helios Health
